note: The Welsh article dates the monument only to the end of the Neolithic and the start of the Bronze Age, and the scheduled-monument list says only "Prehistoric"; no source gives a year, century or millennium for it.

No source dates Yanaque - Quilcamarca. The English article calls the two places legendary villages on the mountain Yanaque and a neighbouring mountain and describes the stone structures and tombs in their ruins, but states no year, century or millennium for their occupation, so the field stays empty.
No source found prints a point for The Street: Wikipedia and Wikidata give none, the Derbyshire HER gives only OS grid references for sections of the route, which are not read.

The Derbyshire HER gives only the period band 'Roman - 43 AD to 409 AD' and Wikipedia no construction year; the years found (1415, 1613, 963) are documentary mentions, not a date for the road's start.

German Wikipedia says the founding date of the theatre is not transmitted ('Das Gründungsdatum des Theaters ist nicht überliefert, vielleicht wurde es schon unter Alexander dem Großen errichtet') and Livius only says it was built by Alexander the Great without a year, so no source dates the start.

The University of Arizona abstract only says the monument has a 'revised early Twenty-Fifth Dynasty dating', a dynasty name without a year, century or millennium; the Vici note dates the official Khonsuirdis (c. 630 BC), not the building, and contradicts it. No readable source gives a start year for the temple.

Wikipedia calls Burley Wood (north of Lydford, Devon) an Iron Age hill fort, a period word without a year or century; the Dartmoor table lists no date for it and the Historic England entry cannot be read, so no source dates the start.

English Wikipedia says only that Justinian I repaired and moved the settlement, with no century or year; the Epirus (Roman province) article places Justinian's reconstruction programme after raids of 548-551 without dating this foundation; the only dated statement (6th century AD) is on Archiqoo, an aggregator site that restates Wikipedia and is not a usable source.
No source gives a year, century or millennium for the start of Ayawayq'u; the paintings are only classed as late or Inca rock art, a period word without a date.

The English and Corsican Wikipedia articles and the Wikidata item print no coordinates for Currachjaghju (Curacchiaghju, Levie), and no readable independent source with a point for the site was found; the stored point stays.

Only class-wide ranges (the Corsican Neolithic, 6000-3000 BC) and period words (Early Neolithic, Prenéolithique) were found for the Curacchiaghju shelter; no source gives a year, century or millennium for the start of this site's occupation.
No readable page prints a point for the so-called Hellenistic House of Nea Paphos; Wikidata has no item for it and the excavation reports and articles found give no coordinates.
Neither the English Wikipedia article nor the MINCETUR-based Turismo Peruano record gives any year, century or period for the Qaqapatan paintings; nothing dates the start.

The Spanish Wikipedia article on the El Conchalito archaeological site (La Paz, Baja California Sur) prints no coordinates, its Wikidata item has none, and no other readable page found gives a point for the site itself.
Wikipedia, Historic England and Peak District Online give only the period word Iron Age or the class range of promontory forts; no readable source dates Castle Naze's own start.
Only the MINCETUR record (in Spanish) calls it a ciudadela subterranea; Wikipedia says only archaeological site, so no English type word can be quoted for a specific type.
Wikipedia and the Victorian fact sheet give no year, century or millennium for the Carisbrook arrangement's construction; the fact sheet says its purpose is unknown.

The stored Kültür Envanteri page for Issium Kalesi gives only the name, region and status, and no coordinate pair; Nominatim returns no match for the fortress. No source I could read quotes a point for the site, so the stored point stays unsourced.
The Kültür Envanteri entry for Issium Kalesi names no period, century or year, and no other readable source I found dates the fortress. Nothing attests its start.
No readable source gives a founding or first-occupation date for Nagara; Wikipedia's only date (2nd century CE creations at Tapa Shotor) concerns Hadda, and the Dionysus foundation story is legend.

Wikipedia says only that Bilbao was occupied since the Preclassic and that its main occupation was Late Classic (c. AD 600-800); Parsons' Middle Classic colony date (c. 400-550) is contested by Popenoe de Hatch's redating. No source dates the start of this site with a year.

German Wikipedia gives only a rounded point (17 19 N, 91 9 W) about 2 km from the stored point, too coarse to confirm or replace it; the INAH/SIC registry record carries the coordinates only in a map link, not in readable text.

The sources found give only period words: Spanish Wikipedia and the Cajamarca regional tourism page call it Chavin-influenced and pre-Inca, and a Zenodo paper places the chullpa in the Middle Horizon; none states a year, century or millennium for the start.
No source found dates Aya Muqu; Wikipedia (English, Spanish, French) only gives its heritage declaration in 2003 and its district.

No source of record dates the windmills' start: the sources give only 'about 1,000 years old', a Safavid style label or 'unknown century', which are not a year, century or millennium for this complex.

No readable page prints a point for Los Pinchudos: the English, Spanish and Russian Wikipedia articles and the Wikidata item carry no coordinates, the World Monuments Fund page is not readable without script, and the Spanish pages found give no coordinates. OpenStreetMap shows a node about 2 km from the stored point, but that is not quotable.

The only readable points (English Wikipedia, Wikidata) are labelled as the mountain's summit; the archaeological site is described by Arkush and Ikehara (closed-access Nawpa Pacha paper) as a small outpost on a spur of Cerro Pucarani about 1 km from Pucarani, and no readable page prints the site's own point, so none can be quoted for the site.

English and Spanish Wikipedia only say the archaeological site was declared National Cultural Heritage and give no date; the paper that mentions Ticona or Inticancha dates the neighbouring Pucarani (AD 1400-1490), not this outpost, and its pages cannot be read by plain GET.
The English and German Wikipedia articles and the Wikidata item for Pigi Athinas carry no coordinates, and no other readable page gives a point for the site; the stored point stays.
The English article of the item gives no year, century or millennium for Uskallaqta and the Wikidata item states no inception, so no source dates the start of the site.
